answer: Rubric rotation: each of the 7 seats gets a sealed emphasis drawn from 4 (cost figures, named weakness, cheapest bypass, checkable rule), revealed at close. A template tuned to a known rubric passes a seat with p = 0.9 on the emphases it copies, 0.1 on the rest; covering two of four gives 0.5 per seat, so P(at least 4 of 7) = 50 %, against 99.7 % for an answer solid on all four. Recycled scaffolding, a thread of copied openers, loses. Cheapest bypass: one seat leaking its emphasis, bought at the zenith of the Established set or from a lagoon of rented wallets.
